demand = [5, 10]

A set of jobs `Jobs` need to be processed on a set of machines `Machines` in series. All jobs have the same processing order through all the machines from machine 1 to machine M. import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(env):
    # Parameters
    jobs = [1, 2, 3]
    machines = [1, 2]
    proces_time = [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]]
    
    model = gp.Model("makespan_minimization", env=env)
    
    # Decision variables
    start_time = model.addVars(len(jobs), len(machines), name="start_time")
    makespan = model.addVar(name="makespan")
    
    # Objective
    model.setObjective(makespan, GRB.MINIMIZE)
    
    # Constraints
    for j in range(len(jobs)):
        for m in range(len(machines)):
            # Constraint for machine sequence
            if m > 0:
                model.addConstr(start_time[j, m] >= start_time[j, m-1] + proces_time[j][m-1])
            # Constraint for job sequence on the same machine
            if j > 0:
                model.addConstr(start_time[j, m] >= start_time[j-1, m] + proces_time[j-1][m])
            # Makespan constraint
            model.addConstr(makespan >= start_time[j, m] + proces_time[j][m])
    
    model.optimize()
    
    # Check if optimal
    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(env):
    # Parameters
    jobs = [1, 2, 3]
    machines = [1, 2]
    proces_time = [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]]
    
    model = gp.Model("makespan_minimization", env=env)
    
    # Decision variables
    start_time = model.addVars(len(jobs), len(machines), name="start_time")
    makespan = model.addVar(name="makespan")
    
    # Objective
    model.setObjective(makespan, GRB.MINIMIZE)
    
    # Constraints
    for j in range(len(jobs)):
        for m in range(len(machines)):
            # Constraint for machine sequence
            if m > 0:
                model.addConstr(start_time[j, m] >= start_time[j, m-1] + proces_time[j][m-1])
            # Constraint for job sequence on the same machine
            if j > 0:
                model.addConstr(start_time[j, m] >= start_time[j-1, m] + proces_time[j-1][m])
            # Makespan constraint
            model.addConstr(makespan >= start_time[j, m] + proces_time[j][m])
    
    model.optimize()
    
    # Check if optimal
    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

The cost of shipping one unit of product `p` from origin `i` to destination `j` is `ShippingCost_{i, j, p}`. The problem aims to minimize the total cost of shipping all products from the origins to the destinations. import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Parameters
supply = [[20, 30], [40, 10]]
demand = [[30, 30], [30, 10]]
limit = [[35, 25], [25, 30]]
cost = [[[2, 3], [4, 1]], [[3, 2], [2, 4]]]

# Sets
origins = range(len(supply))
destinations = range(len(demand))
products = range(len(supply[0]))

# Create model
model = gp.Model("multi_commodity_transportation")

# Variables
x = model.addVars(origins, destinations, products, name="x")

# Objective
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(x[i, j, p] * cost[i][j][p] for i in origins for j in destinations for p in products), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Supply constraints
for i in origins:
    for p in products:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j, p] for j in destinations) == supply[i][p], name=f"supply_{i}_{p}")

# Demand constraints
for j in destinations:
    for p in products:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j, p] for i in origins) == demand[j][p], name=f"demand_{j}_{p}")

# Limit constraints
for i in origins:
    for j in destinations:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j, p] for p in products) <= limit[i][j], name=f"limit_{i}_{j}")

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Check if optimal and print
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

    "cost": [2, 3, 1.5],

    "f_max": [100, 100, 100],
    "n_min": [50, 60],

}

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Check if optimal and print
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve_transportation_problem(env):
    # Parameters
    Cities = ["A", "B"]
    Links = [["A", "B"]]
    Products = ["Product1"]
    Supply = [[10], [0]]
    Demand = [[0], [10]]
    ShipmentCost = [[[1]]]
    Capacity = [[[10]]]
    JointCapacity = [[10]]

    # Convert Links to tuples
    links = [tuple(link) for link in Links]
    num_links = len(links)
    num_products = len(Products)

    # Create model
    model = gp.Model(env=env)

    # Create variables
    x = model.addVars(links, range(num_products), name="x", vtype=GRB.INTEGER)

    # Objective function
    obj = gp.quicksum(
        ShipmentCost[link_index][p][0] * x[link, p]
        for link_index, link in enumerate(links)
        for p in range(num_products)
    )
    model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Flow balance constraints
    for i in range(len(Cities)):
        city = Cities[i]
        for p in range(num_products):
            flow_balance = Supply[i][p] - Demand[i][p]
            outgoing_flow = 0
            incoming_flow = 0
            for link in links:
                if link[0] == city:
                    outgoing_flow += x[link, p]
                if link[1] == city:
                    incoming_flow += x[link, p]
            model.addConstr(outgoing_flow - incoming_flow == flow_balance, name=f"flow_balance_{i}_{p}")

    # Capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):
        for p in range(num_products):
            capacity = Capacity[link_index][p][0]
            model.addConstr(x[link, p] <= capacity, name=f"capacity_{link_index}_{p}")

    # Joint capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):
        joint_capacity = JointCapacity[link_index][0]
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[link, p] for p in range(num_products)) <= joint_capacity, name=f"joint_capacity_{link_index}")

    # Optimize
    model.optimize()

    # Check if optimal
    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve_transportation_problem(env):
    # Parameters
    Cities = ["A", "B"]
    Links = [["A", "B"]]
    Products = ["Product1"]
    Supply = [[10], [0]]
    Demand = [[0], [10]]
    ShipmentCost = [[[1]]]
    Capacity = [[[10]]]
    JointCapacity = [[10]]

    # Convert Links to tuples
    links = [tuple(link) for link in Links]
    num_links = len(links)
    num_products = len(Products)

    # Create model
    model = gp.Model(env=env)

    # Create variables
    x = model.addVars(links, range(num_products), name="x", vtype=GRB.INTEGER)

    # Objective function
    obj = gp.quicksum(
        ShipmentCost[link_index][p][0] * x[link, p]
        for link_index, link in enumerate(links)
        for p in range(num_products)
    )
    model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Flow balance constraints
    for i in range(len(Cities)):
        city = Cities[i]
        for p in range(num_products):
            flow_balance = Supply[i][p] - Demand[i][p]
            outgoing_flow = 0
            incoming_flow = 0
            for link in links:
                if link[0] == city:
                    outgoing_flow += x[link, p]
                if link[1] == city:
                    incoming_flow += x[link, p]
            model.addConstr(outgoing_flow - incoming_flow == flow_balance, name=f"flow_balance_{i}_{p}")

    # Capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):
        for p in range(num_products):
            capacity = Capacity[link_index][p][0]
            model.addConstr(x[link, p] <= capacity, name=f"capacity_{link_index}_{p}")

    # Joint capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):
        joint_capacity = JointCapacity[link_index][0]
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[link, p] for p in range(num_products)) <= joint_capacity, name=f"joint_capacity_{link_index}")

    # Optimize
    model.optimize()

    # Check if optimal
    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        # Print the final objective
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
    else:
        # If not optimal, do not print anything
        pass

    return model

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve_transportation_problem(env):
    # Parameters
    Cities = ["A", "B"]
    Links = [["A", "B"]]
    Products = ["Product1"]
    Supply = [[10], [0]]
    Demand = [[0], [10]]
    ShipmentCost = [[[1]]]
    Capacity = [[[10]]]
    JointCapacity = [[10]]

    # Convert Links to tuples
    links = [tuple(link) for link in Links]
    num_links = len(links)
    num_products = len(Products)

    # Create model
    model = gp.Model(env=env)

    # Create variables
    x = model.addVars(links, range(num_products), name="x", vtype=GRB.INTEGER)

    # Objective function
    obj = gp.quicksum(
        ShipmentCost[link_index][p][0] * x[link, p]
        for link_index, link in enumerate(links)
        for p in range(num_products)
    )
    model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Flow balance constraints
    for i in range(len(Cities)):
        city = Cities[i]
        for p in range(num_products):
            flow_balance = Supply[i][p] - Demand[i][p]
            outgoing_flow = 0
            incoming_flow = 0
            for link in links:
                if link[0] == city:
                    outgoing_flow += x[link, p]
                if link[1] == city:
                    incoming_flow += x[link, p]
            model.addConstr(outgoing_flow - incoming_flow == flow_balance, name=f"flow_balance_{i}_{p}")

    # Capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):
        for p in range(num_products):
            capacity = Capacity[link_index][p][0]
            model.addConstr(x[link, p] <= capacity, name=f"capacity_{link_index}_{p}")

    # Joint capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):
        joint_capacity = JointCapacity[link_index][0]
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[link, p] for p in range(num_products)) <= joint_capacity, name=f"joint_capacity_{link_index}")

    # Optimize
    model.optimize()

    # Check if optimal
    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

def solve_transportation_problem(env):

    Demand = [[0], [10]]
    ShipmentCost = [[[1]]]
    Capacity = [[[10]]]
    JointCapacity = [[10]]

    links = [tuple(link) for link in Links]
    num_links = len(links)
    num_products = len(Products)

    x = model.addVars(links, range(num_products), name="x", vtype=GRB.INTEGER)

    # Objective function
    obj = gp.quicksum(
        ShipmentCost[link_index][p][0] * x[link, p]
        for link_index, link in enumerate(links)
        for p in range(num_products)
    )
    model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Flow balance constraints
    for i in range(len(Cities)):
        city = Cities[i]
        for p in range(num_products):
            flow_balance = Supply[i][p] - Demand[i][p]
            outgoing_flow = 0
            incoming_flow = 0
            for link in links:
                if link[0] == city:
                    outgoing_flow += x[link, p]
                if link[1] == city:
                    incoming_flow += x[link, p]
            model.addConstr(outgoing_flow - incoming_flow == flow_balance, name=f"flow_balance_{i}_{p}")

    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):

    # Joint capacity constraints
    for link_index, link in enumerate(links):

        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[link, p] for p in range(num_products)) <= joint_capacity, name=f"joint_capacity_{link_index}")

    model.optimize()

        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Parameters
alloys_on_market = [0, 1]
required_elements = ["A", "B"]
composition_data = [[0.5, 0.1], [0.5, 0.9]]
desired_blend_percentage = [0.5, 0.5]
alloy_price = [10.0, 20.0]

# Create model
env = gp.Env()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(len(alloys_on_market), name="x", lb=0, ub=GRB.INFINITY)

# Objective: minimize total cost
model.setObjective(sum(alloy_price[alloy] * x[alloy] for alloy in alloys_on_market), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Constraints: blend percentage for each element
for element in range(len(required_elements)):
    model.addConstr(sum(composition_data[alloy][element] * x[alloy] for alloy in alloys_on_market) == desired_blend_percentage[element], name=f"blend_{element}")

# Constraint: total amount is 1
model.addConstr(sum(x) == 1, name="total_amount")

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the final objective if optimal
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

participants = ["P1", "P2", "P3"]
cars = ["C1", "C2", "C3"]
possible_assignments = [[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 1]]

# Create model
env = gp.Env()
model = gp.Model("CarSelection", env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(len(participants), len(cars), vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

# Objective: maximize total assignments
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in range(len(participants)) for j in range(len(cars))), GRB.MAXIMIZE)

# Constraints: x[i,j] <= possible_assignments[i][j]
for i in range(len(participants)):
    for j in range(len(cars)):
        model.addConstr(x[i, j] <= possible_assignments[i][j], name=f"constraint_{i}_{j}")

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the final objective
print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Parameters
availability = [2, 3, 1]
demand = [100, 150]
capabilities = [[50, 70], [60, 80], [70, 90]]
costs = [[100, 200], [150, 250], [200, 300]]

# Create the model
env = gp.Env()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: x[i][j] = number of aircraft type i assigned to route j
x = model.addVars(3, 2, name="x", lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER)

# Demand constraints: total capacity for each route must meet demand
for j in range(2):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i][j] * capabilities[i][j] for i in range(3)) >= demand[j])

# Availability constraints: total aircraft of each type assigned cannot exceed availability
for i in range(3):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i][j] for j in range(2)) <= availability[i])

# Objective: minimize total cost
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(x[i][j] * costs[i][j] for i in range(3) for j in range(2)), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the result if optimal
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

The main media selection problem is a problem of allocating advertising budgets between possible advertising outlets. Given a set of media options, it aims to determine which media should be selected so that all audiences are reached with minimum campaign cost. It does not matter if an audience is covered more than once, as long as it is covered at least once. Moreover, the company does not wish to spend more money on the campaign than necessary.
Parameters: {"target_audiences": [0, 1, 2], "advertising_media": [0, 1, 2], "incidence_matrix": [[1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1]], "media_costs": [10, 15, 20]}

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Problem parameters
target_audiences = [0, 1, 2]
advertising_media = [0, 1, 2]
incidence_matrix = [[1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1]]
media_costs = [10, 15, 20]

# Create model
env = gp.Env()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: x[i] = 1 if media i is selected, 0 otherwise
x = model.addVars(len(advertising_media), vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

# Constraints: Each audience must be covered by at least one selected media
for audience in target_audiences:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(incidence_matrix[audience][media] * x[media] for media in range(len(advertising_media))) >= 1)

# Objective: Minimize total cost
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(media_costs[media] * x[media] for media in range(len(media_costs))), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

Input

A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X

limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.

```python

A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X

A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive

limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.

EXAMPLE 1
=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 2
=========

Input
-----
An energy company chooses nonnegative integer numbers of solar and wind
projects. A solar project costs 7 units and a wind project costs 5 units. The
portfolio must satisfy 2 solar + 3 wind >= 10, while grid capacity requires
4 solar + wind <= 15. What is the minimum total investment cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
solar = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="solar")
wind = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="wind")
model.addConstr(2 * solar + 3 * wind >= 10, name="minimum_output")
model.addConstr(4 * solar + wind <= 15, name="grid_capacity")
model.setObjective(7 * solar + 5 * wind, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

You receive one optimization problem at a time. Preserve every datum, unit,
index, time convention, logical condition, objective direction, and requested
output quantity from the problem statement. Work only with the information in
the supplied inputs. Do not ask questions or use external tools.

stages.user_prompt:
INPUT
-----
You receive one natural-language operations-research problem.

TASK
----
Translate the problem into one complete Python program using gurobipy and solve
the requested objective.

STEP 1: Build the model
-----------------------
Extract the sets, parameters, decision variables and domains, objective, and
constraints. Encode every numerical datum from the statement directly.

STEP 2: Apply implementation rules
-----------------------------------
- Import gurobipy as gp and GRB.
- Create the model with the runtime-provided environment exactly as
  gp.Model(env=env).
- Preserve objective direction, units, indexing, integrality, and all logical
  or temporal restrictions.
- Call model.optimize().

STEP 3: Produce the final output
--------------------------------
Return only one Python program, optionally inside one python code fence. If and
only if the requested solution is available and optimal, print exactly one line
FINAL_OBJECTIVE=<finite numeric value>.

RULES
-----
Do not read or write files, access the network, spawn processes, install
packages, call input(), use dynamic evaluation, or revise the model after an
error. The caller performs policy checking and solver verification separately.

FEW-SHOT DEMONSTRATIONS

EXAMPLE 1
=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 2
=========

Input
-----
An energy company chooses nonnegative integer numbers of solar and wind
projects. A solar project costs 7 units and a wind project costs 5 units. The
portfolio must satisfy 2 solar + 3 wind >= 10, while grid capacity requires
4 solar + wind <= 15. What is the minimum total investment cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
solar = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="solar")
wind = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="wind")
model.addConstr(2 * solar + 3 * wind >= 10, name="minimum_output")
model.addConstr(4 * solar + wind <= 15, name="grid_capacity")
model.setObjective(7 * solar + 5 * wind, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

END FEW-SHOT DEMONSTRATIONS

TARGET PROBLEM
--------------
Consider a production problem. Given a set of products `Products` and a set of stages `Stages`. Each product `p` has a certain production rate `Rate_{p, s}` in each stage `s` and a certain profit `Profit_{p}` per ton. Each stage `s` has a certain number of hours `Available_{s}` available per week. There are also lower and upper limits on the tons of each product sold in a week, `Commit_{p}` and `Market_{p}` respectively. The problem aims to maximize the total profit from all products. It is constrained that the total number of hours used by all products in each stage `s` may not exceed the hours available. How to decide the number of tons to be produced for each product `p`?
Parameters: {"products": ["P1", "P2"], "stages": ["S1", "S2"], "rate": [[2, 3], [3, 2]], "profit": [10, 20], "commit": [1, 2], "market": [5, 4], "avail": [10, 8]}

model = gp.Model(env=env)
products = ["P1", "P2"]
stages = ["S1", "S2"]
rate = [[2, 3], [3, 2]]
profit = [10, 20]
commit = [1, 2]
market = [5, 4]
avail = [10, 8]

x = model.addVars(products, lb=commit, ub=market, name="x")

for s in range(len(stages)):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(rate[p][s] * x[p] for p in products) <= avail[s], name=f"stage_{stages[s]}")

model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(profit[p] * x[p] for p in products), GRB.MAXIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 1
=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 2
=========

Input
-----
An energy company chooses nonnegative integer numbers of solar and wind
projects. A solar project costs 7 units and a wind project costs 5 units. The
portfolio must satisfy 2 solar + 3 wind >= 10, while grid capacity requires
4 solar + wind <= 15. What is the minimum total investment cost?

-----------------

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:

```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
participants = ["P1", "P2", "P3"]
cars = ["C1", "C2", "C3"]
possible_assignments = [[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 1]]

x = model.addVars(participants, cars, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

for i in range(len(participants)):
    for j in range(len(cars)):
        model.addConstr(x[participants[i], cars[j]] <= possible_assignments[i][j])

model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in participants for j in cars), GRB.MAXIMIZE)

    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

model = gp.Model(env=env)

availability = [2, 3, 1]
demand = [100, 150]
capabilities = [[50, 70], [60, 80], [70, 90]]
costs = [[100, 200], [150, 250], [200, 300]]

aircraft_types = len(availability)
routes = len(demand)
x = model.addVars(aircraft_types, routes, name="x", vtype=GRB.INTEGER, lb=0)

for i in range(aircraft_types):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(routes)) <= availability[i], name=f"availability_{i}")

for j in range(routes):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] * capabilities[i][j] for i in range(aircraft_types)) >= demand[j], name=f"demand_{j}")

model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] * costs[i][j] for i in range(aircraft_types) for j in range(routes)), GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```
